The Ideology of the Ideology-Free
We are taught that the United States is uniquely free of
ideological teachings. Yet, our political culture is heavily
fortified by "idols"-myths about the free market,
superpatriotism, and a classless society.
These are not natural truths; they are meticulously
constructed ideologies that serve conservative class
interests and suppress democratic struggle.

The Politics of Religiosity
Elite Religiosity
• Views God as a partisan punisher and material
benefactor.
• Preaches obedience and attributes poverty to
personal sin or flawed character.
• Utilizes tax-free corporate accumulation to
protect the wealth of oligarchs.
Liberation Theology

Piercing the Façade:
The Dirty Secret of Class
Modern media freely discusses taboo subjects,
yet 'class' remains heavily censored.
Acknowledging class power is a subversive act
because it threatens the core mechanism of
the capitalist system: the continuous upward
transfer of wealth.

The Balance of Power: A Blueprint of Extraction.
COLUMN A: The Few
The Working Class (98%)
Live principally by selling their labor.
Earned Income: Wages, Salaries, Pensions.
COLUMN B: The Many
The Owning Class (2%)
Live principally off other people's
labor.
Unearned Income: Dividends,
Interest, Capital Gains, Rents.
Capital cannot create anything on its own. The immense wealth of Column A rests
entirely on the continuous expropriation of the labor generated by Column B.

Redefining Class: Identity vs. Exploitation
The Class Definition Matrix
The Mainstream (Weberian) View
Defines class as a static demographic label
(income, status, blue-collar vs. white-collar).
It views classes as disconnected lifestyle buckets.
Purpose: To hide the conflict.
Income

The Marxist View

Breaking the Idols
Inn
Ruling class hegemony is powerful, but imperfect. It
relies entirely on the illusion of our consent. Once the
idols are recognized as manufactured myths designed to
mask class exploitation, that consent can be withdrawn.
True patriotism is not quietism. It is the active,
class-conscious struggle to dismantle monopoly
culture and reclaim the economic, cultural, and
political life of the people.
